root.label: The Cold War, 1945–1991
root.gloss: Ideological division, Yalta to Berlin, Cuban nuclear brinkmanship, Asian proxy wars, Soviet collapse, and Global South reassessment.

children.label: Part 1: Origins & Divided Europe
children.gloss: Capitalist vs Communist rivalry, Yalta and Potsdam, containment, the Berlin Airlift, and NATO vs the Warsaw Pact.

children.label: 1. Capitalism vs Communism
children.gloss: Incompatible ideologies, interwar grievances, America’s 1945 atomic monopoly, and Europe’s post-war power vacuum.

children.label: Rival Ideas & Pre-1945 Distrust
children.gloss: US democratic capitalism clashed with Soviet one-party communism, deepened by 1917 intervention and the 1939 Nazi-Soviet Pact.

children.label: Free Market vs Command Socialism
children.gloss: US private business, multi-party votes; Soviet Politburo ran state farms.

children.label: 1917 Intervention & 1939 Pact
children.gloss: West backed anti-Bolshevik White armies; Stalin divided Poland with Hitler.

children.label: → Broke Wartime Alliance Once Hitler Fell
children.gloss: Common Nazi enemy disappeared 1945; Old grievances returned with force.

children.label: Each Viewed Rival System Tyrannical
children.gloss: US condemned one-party Soviet rule; Moscow called Western democracy sham.

children.label: Atomic Monopoly & Arms Race
children.gloss: Trinity, Hiroshima, and Nagasaki gave Washington a nuclear monopoly that Stalin countered with a crash Soviet bomb programme.

children.label: Trinity Test, Hiroshima & Nagasaki
children.gloss: Tested New Mexico 16 July; Dropped two bombs August 1945.

children.label: Stalin Feared US Atomic Blackmail
children.gloss: Held temporary US nuclear monopoly; Viewed as intimidation over Europe.

children.label: → Ordered Crash Soviet Bomb Project
children.gloss: Pushed Soviet physicists top speed; Sparked dangerous nuclear arms race.

children.label: Created Post-War Balance of Terror
children.gloss: Transformed diplomacy with atomic dread; Replaced trust with deterrence.

children.label: Ruined Europe’s Power Vacuum
children.gloss: Meeting along the River Elbe across ruined Europe, US and Soviet forces locked the continent into bipolar rivalry.

children.label: WWII Shattered Old European Powers
children.gloss: Left vast continental power vacuum; Red Army met Western Allies.

children.label: Security Moves Read as Aggression
children.gloss: Both superpowers sought border security; Misread rival defences as threats.

children.label: → Divided East-West Spheres Hardened
children.gloss: Replaced older multi-power diplomacy; Split continent into rival camps.

children.label: Peace Impossible, Total War Unlikely
children.gloss: Raymond Aron summed deadlock up; Nuclear fear blocked open war.

children.label: 2. From Yalta to Potsdam
children.gloss: Yalta compromises unravelled over Poland, new leaders Truman and Attlee, atomic leverage, and German reparations at Potsdam.

children.label: Yalta Deal & Polish Dispute
children.gloss: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin agreed four German zones at Yalta, but Stalin installed the communist Lublin Poles.

children.label: Feb 1945 Yalta Four-Zone Deal
children.gloss: Divided Germany and Berlin fourfold; Stalin joined UN, Japan war.

children.label: 27m Soviet Dead & Buffer Demand
children.gloss: Demanded friendly Polish border zone; Installed communist Lublin Polish regime.

children.label: → Sidelined Exiled Democratic London Poles
children.gloss: Broke Declaration on Liberated Europe; Wrecked Western trust in Stalin.

children.label: Poland Exposed Fragile Yalta Smiles
children.gloss: UK entered WWII for Poland; Clashed with Soviet security belt.

children.label: Potsdam Guard Change & Bomb Hint
children.gloss: Anti-communist Truman and Labour PM Attlee met Stalin at Potsdam as Truman hinted at America’s newly tested atomic weapon.

children.label: Truman & Attlee Replaced Wartime Pair
children.gloss: Roosevelt died April; Truman hardened; Attlee replaced Churchill mid-summit.

children.label: Truman’s 24 July Atomic Hint
children.gloss: Trinity exploded 16 July eve; Soviet spies already briefed Stalin.

children.label: → Convinced Stalin US Meant Bullying
children.gloss: Hoped bomb forced Soviet concessions; Deepened Kremlin suspicion and defiance.

children.label: Turned Summit Diplomacy Openly Bitter
children.gloss: Only Stalin remained from Yalta; Ended wartime personal rapport.

children.label: Reparations Clash & Zone Split
children.gloss: Disputes over Stalin’s $20 billion reparations demand restricted extractions to each occupier’s zone, ending the Grand Alliance.

children.label: Stalin Demanded $20bn Reparations
children.gloss: Wanted $10bn straight for USSR; West recalled 1919 Weimar ruin.

children.label: Own-Zone Reparations Compromise
children.gloss: Each power took from zone; Traded eastern food for machinery.

children.label: → Killed Wartime Grand Alliance
children.gloss: Split German economic administration early; Hardened rival spheres across Europe.

children.label: Set Stage for Divided Germany
children.gloss: Turned temporary zones semi-permanent; Prepared 1948 Berlin confrontation.

children.label: 3. Iron Curtain & Berlin Airlift
children.gloss: Churchill’s Fulton speech, Truman Doctrine and Marshall Aid, Cominform, the 324-day Berlin Airlift, and NATO vs Warsaw Pact.

children.label: Iron Curtain & US Containment
children.gloss: Soviet salami tactics prompted Churchill’s Fulton warning, the March 1947 Truman Doctrine, and over $13bn in Marshall Aid.

children.label: Salami Tactics & Fulton Speech
children.gloss: Rákosi sliced rival parties away; Churchill warned Iron Curtain 1946.

children.label: Truman Doctrine & $13bn Marshall Plan
children.gloss: Backed Greece and Turkey 1947; Over $13bn rebuilt Western Europe.

children.label: → Provoked Cominform & Aid Ban
children.gloss: Stalin branded aid dollar imperialism; Barred eastern satellites taking dollars.

children.label: Enacted Official US Containment Policy
children.gloss: Ended traditional peacetime US isolation; Fought communism through economic recovery.

children.label: Prague Coup & Berlin Airlift
children.gloss: After the 1948 Prague Coup and Trizonia’s Deutsche Mark, Allied planes defeated Stalin’s 324-day Berlin Blockade.

children.label: Prague Coup & New Deutsche Mark
children.gloss: Czech communists seized Prague Feb; West merged Trizonia, new currency.

children.label: 24 June Blockade vs 324-Day Airlift
children.gloss: Stalin cut road, rail, canals; Flew 2.3m tons food, coal.

children.label: → Stalin Lifted Blockade May 1949
children.gloss: Clay and Bevin sustained Berliners; Defeated blockade without firing shots.

children.label: First Major Cold War Victory
children.gloss: Proved Western resolve over Berlin; Made peaceful German unity impossible.

children.label: FRG, GDR, NATO & Warsaw Pact
children.gloss: The Berlin crisis split Germany into FRG and GDR in 1949 and locked Europe into rival NATO (1949) and Warsaw Pact (1955) alliances.

children.label: 1949 Creation of FRG & GDR
children.gloss: Democratic West Germany capital Bonn; Communist East Germany formed October.

children.label: 1949 NATO & 1955 Warsaw Pact
children.gloss: Twelve Western allies founded NATO; Seven eastern states joined Moscow.

children.label: → Froze Armed Frontier Across Europe
children.gloss: Triggered after FRG joined NATO; Guaranteed mutual defence if attacked.

children.label: Shifted Hot Conflict Outside Europe
children.gloss: Deterrence stabilised European bloc borders; Displaced superpower wars to Asia.

children.label: Part 2: Brinkmanship & Asia Wars
children.gloss: Thirteen days on the nuclear brink over Cuba (1962) and deadly Cold War proxy wars in Korea and Vietnam (1950–75).

children.label: 4. Cuban Missile Crisis
children.gloss: Castro’s revolution, Bay of Pigs, U-2 missile photos, Kennedy’s quarantine, secret Turkey diplomacy, and the 1963 Hotline.

children.label: Castro, Bay of Pigs & Anadyr
children.gloss: US embargoes and the failed Bay of Pigs pushed Castro toward Khrushchev, whose Operation Anadyr missiles U-2 planes spotted.

children.label: 1959 Castro & Bay of Pigs Fiasco
children.gloss: Nationalised US sugar, oil, phones; Crushed 1,400 CIA exiles 1961.

children.label: Operation Anadyr & U-2 Discovery
children.gloss: Countered 17:1 ICBM, Turkey Jupiters; Heyser’s U-2 spotted sites 14 Oct.

children.label: → Put US Cities 3 Minutes Away
children.gloss: 40,000 Soviet troops inside Cuba; Sparked Kennedy’s 13-day ExComm crisis.

children.label: Boldest Gamble of Nuclear Brinkmanship
children.gloss: Placed Soviet warheads 90 miles; Tested American resolve directly.

children.label: Quarantine & Black Saturday
children.gloss: Kennedy chose a naval quarantine at DEFCON 2 while Vasili Arkhipov prevented nuclear submarine war on Black Saturday.

children.label: 22 Oct Quarantine & DEFCON 2
children.gloss: Rejected generals’ Cuba bombing call; Avoided killing Soviets, spared Berlin.

children.label: 27 Oct U-2 & Vasili Arkhipov
children.gloss: U-2 shot down over Cuba; Arkhipov blocked nuclear sub torpedo.

children.label: → Forced Secret RFK–Dobrynin Deal
children.gloss: Soviet cargo ships turned back; Leaders sought urgent midnight exit.

children.label: Closest World Came to Armageddon
children.gloss: One submarine vote saved millions; Exposed peril of nuclear miscalculation.

children.label: Turkey Swap, Hotline & Test Ban
children.gloss: Removing Cuban and Turkish missiles led to the 1963 Moscow–Washington Hotline and the Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty.

children.label: Cuba Withdrawal & Secret Turkey Deal
children.gloss: USSR pulled Cuba missiles UN-checked; US pledged non-invasion, pulled Jupiters.

children.label: 1963 Hotline & Partial Test Ban
children.gloss: Installed direct teletype leader link; Banned atmospheric, space, underwater tests.

children.label: → Stabilised Superpower Nuclear Deterrence
children.gloss: Signed by US, UK, USSR; Replaced telegram delays with speed.

children.label: MAD Compelled Crisis De-escalation
children.gloss: Both superpowers stepped from brink; Opened path toward arms control.

children.label: 5. Proxy Wars: Korea & Vietnam
children.gloss: Domino Theory and NSC-68 drove US intervention in Korea (1950–53) and Vietnam (1954–75), exposing limits of superpower might.

children.label: Domino Theory & Korean War
children.gloss: Mao’s 1949 victory and NSC-68 framed the 1950–53 Korean War, which left over three million dead along the 38th Parallel.

children.label: 1949 Mao Victory, RDS-1 & NSC-68
children.gloss: Soviet A-bomb and China PRC; Quadrupled US defence; Domino Theory.

children.label: 1950–53 Korean War Seesaw
children.gloss: Kim invaded; MacArthur landed Inchon; Chinese attack restored 38th Parallel.

children.label: → Stalemate With Over 3m Dead
children.gloss: Ended July 1953 at DMZ; Globalised US containment across Asia.

children.label: First Major Hot Proxy Conflict
children.gloss: Soviet tanks fought UN-US troops; Kept nuclear weapons unused.

children.label: Tonkin & Vietcong Guerrilla War
children.gloss: Following Dien Bien Phu and Gulf of Tonkin, Vietcong guerrilla warfare and Cu Chi tunnels blunted 500,000 US troops.

children.label: Dien Bien Phu & 1964 Tonkin
children.gloss: 1954 split Vietnam 17th Parallel; Tonkin brought 500,000+ US troops.

children.label: 250km Cu Chi Tunnels vs Napalm
children.gloss: Booby traps, Ho Chi Minh Trail; US used helicopters, Agent Orange.

children.label: Booby traps, Ho Chi Minh Trail
children.gloss: Booby traps, Ho Chi Minh Trail

children.label: → Civilian Losses Fuelled Anti-War Anger
children.gloss: Turned rural villagers against Saigon; Televised bloodshed sparked US protests.

children.label: Asymmetric Tactics Blunted Superpower Tech
children.gloss: Avoided pitched open US battles; Drained American morale through attrition.

children.label: 1968 Tet & Fall of Saigon
children.gloss: The 1968 Tet Offensive forced Vietnamization and the 1973 US withdrawal before Saigon fell in April 1975.

children.label: Jan 1968 Surprise Tet Offensive
children.gloss: Struck 100+ towns, US Embassy; Shocked American TV viewers home.

children.label: Vietnamization & 1973 Paris Accords
children.gloss: Nixon, Kissinger pulled troops out; Handed combat to South Vietnam.

children.label: → Saigon Fell April 1975
children.gloss: North Vietnamese tanks captured Saigon; United Vietnam under communist rule.

children.label: Exposed Limits of Superpower Hegemony
children.gloss: Nationalist resolve outlasted US wealth; Ended automatic Asian Domino interventions.

children.label: Part 3: Collapse & Global View
children.gloss: The 1961 Berlin Wall, Soviet stagnation and Afghanistan, Gorbachev’s reforms, 9 November 1989, USSR dissolution, and global reassessment.

children.label: 6. Berlin Wall & USSR Collapse
children.gloss: From the 1961 Berlin Wall and Afghan quagmire to Gorbachev’s Sinatra Doctrine, breaching the Wall (1989), and December 1991 dissolution.

children.label: 1961 Wall, Stagnation & Afghan War
children.gloss: Built in 1961 to stop 2.7m defectors, Soviet power stalled under economic stagnation, Afghanistan, and Reagan’s SDI.

children.label: 13 Aug 1961 Berlin Wall Built
children.gloss: 2.7m+ East Germans fled west; Ulbricht halted skilled brain drain.

children.label: Stagnation, Afghanistan & Reagan SDI
children.gloss: Quarter wealth spent on weapons; 1979 Afghan mujahideen; Star Wars.

children.label: → Forced Gorbachev’s 1985 Overhaul
children.gloss: Food queues and lagging computers; Moscow could not afford race.

children.label: Overstretch Drained Command Economy
children.gloss: Wall symbolised communist repression starkly; Ten-year Afghan war bled USSR.

children.label: Gorbachev & 9 Nov 1989 Wall
children.gloss: Glasnost, Perestroika, and the Sinatra Doctrine unleashed 1989 Velvet Revolutions and toppled the Berlin Wall on 9 November.

children.label: Glasnost, Perestroika & Sinatra Policy
children.gloss: Opened free debate, small firms; Scrapped Brezhnev Red Army force.

children.label: Solidarity & 9 Nov Wall Breached
children.gloss: Wałęsa won June; Hungary opened; Schabowski’s live TV blunder opened.

children.label: → Peaceful Revolutions & 1990 Unity
children.gloss: Crowds tore concrete Wall down; Germany reunified peacefully in 1990.

children.label: Ended Forty Years of Eastern Bloc
children.gloss: Removing tank fear toppled regimes; Symbolised triumph of people power.

children.label: 1991 Coup & Soviet Dissolution
children.gloss: Boris Yeltsin defeated hardliners’ August 1991 Moscow coup, hastening republic breakaways and Gorbachev’s Christmas Day resignation.

children.label: Failed August 1991 Hardliner Coup
children.gloss: Arrested Gorbachev inside Crimea villa; Yeltsin rallied crowds atop tank.

children.label: 25 Dec 1991 USSR Dissolved
children.gloss: Fifteen constituent republics voted out; Soviet flag lowered over Kremlin.

children.label: → Ended Forty-Six-Year Cold War
children.gloss: Broke Communist Party rule permanently; Closed superpower bipolar world era.

children.label: Collapsed Superpower Without World War
children.gloss: National movements dismantled Soviet empire; Peaceful collapse stunned world leaders.

children.label: 7. Reassessing the ‘Cold’ War
children.gloss: Challenging the Eurocentric "Long Peace" with 20 million Global South deaths, CIA/KGB covert wars, the Space Race, and MAD.

children.label: Long Peace vs 20m Global Dead
children.gloss: While nuclear deterrence kept European borders calm, proxy wars killed over 20 million people across the Global South.

children.label: Traditional: Gaddis’s European Long Peace
children.gloss: NATO-Warsaw borders stayed stable; Superpowers avoided direct European fire.

children.label: Modern: Eurocentric Myth; 20m Dead
children.gloss: 3m Korea, 2m+ Vietnam perished; Hot wars across Global South.

children.label: → Ruined Post-Colonial Towns & Landmines
children.gloss: Armed dictatorships in Angola, Afghanistan; Left refugees and unexploded mines.

children.label: Decentres Cold War Beyond Europe
children.gloss: Calm Berlin contrasted burning South; Centers Asian, African, Latin voices.

children.label: Covert Coups & Space Race
children.gloss: CIA coups, KGB/Stasi spying, Sputnik 1, and Apollo 11 waged relentless ideological conflict below declared war.

children.label: CIA Coups vs KGB & Stasi
children.gloss: Toppled Iran 1953, Guatemala 1954; Stasi kept millions informant files.

children.label: Sputnik, Gagarin & Apollo 11
children.gloss: 1957 Sputnik, 1961 Yuri Gagarin; NASA landed Moon July 1969.

children.label: → Accelerated Global Missile Arsenals
children.gloss: Rockets doubled as ICBM boosters; Could destroy Earth several times.

children.label: Weaponised Spying & Science Globally
children.gloss: Fought unseen below open war; Turned technology into prestige test.

children.label: MAD & The Synoptic Verdict
children.gloss: Mutually Assured Destruction prevented direct superpower armageddon even as proxy bloodshed persisted through 1970s détente.

children.label: MAD Made Direct War Suicide
children.gloss: Guaranteed mutual nuclear annihilation; Stopped direct Washington-Moscow combat.

children.label: 1970s Détente Slowed Arms Only
children.gloss: Brief missile treaties eased tension; Operation Ajax, Dirty Wars continued.

children.label: → Kept Europe Cold, South Burning
children.gloss: Exported arms across poorer nations; Bloodshed spanned four continents.

children.label: Total Ideological Struggle Without WWIII
children.gloss: Shaped half-century of world order; Proved deterrence spared superpowers alone.
